settings.remove.title: Remove Kleaner
settings.remove.what: Erases all Kleaner data: the log and preferences (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kleaner and %LOCALAPPDATA%\com.swaksm.kleaner folders). Kleaner then closes.
settings.remove.exe: Kleaner is portable: there is nothing else to uninstall. Then just delete the kleaner.exe file.
settings.remove.irreversible: The log will be permanently lost. Your files and programs are not touched.
disclaimer.title: Before you start
disclaimer.does: Kleaner scans your drives and shows you what takes up space, hidden files included.
disclaimer.never: It never does anything without your confirmation. It never touches your passwords, cookies, sessions or the registry.
disclaimer.network: No Internet connection: nothing is sent, no telemetry.
disclaimer.caches: Caches and temporary files are permanently deleted (they rebuild themselves). Your personal files always go to the Recycle Bin.
disclaimer.journal: Every action is written to a readable log: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Kleaner\journal.log.
disclaimer.license: Free software under the MIT license, provided without warranty. You remain responsible for what you delete.
journal.intro: Everything Kleaner did on this PC, newest first.
analyse.intro: Kleaner scans the drives you tick, hidden files included, to show you what takes up space. Nothing is changed during the scan.
analyse.topFilesHint: Tick the files you no longer need to send them to the Recycle Bin.
trash.title: Send to the Recycle Bin?
trash.mode: Mode: Recycle Bin. Files stay recoverable.
trash.space: Space is freed when you empty the Recycle Bin.
trash.done: sent to the Recycle Bin. Empty it to free the space.
cleanup.intro: Kleaner estimated what can be removed without changing how you use your PC. Nothing is ticked in advance: choose yourself, or tick the risk-free items in one click.
cleanup.skippedWhy: Skipped files were in use by an open app. Try again after closing it.
cleanup.permanent: Permanent deletion: these files do not go to the Recycle Bin.
cleanup.heavyIntro: These cleanups free a lot of space but have a consequence. Each one asks for its own confirmation.
cleanup.heavyAckHint: Tick the box to be able to run it.
admin.why: System cleanups and some folders need admin rights.
programs.intro: Installed programs. Measured size: real space of the install folder on disk. Declared size: what the program reports to Windows (often missing or wrong). Kleaner only launches their official uninstaller.
programs.confirm: Kleaner will launch this program’s official uninstaller. Follow its steps; the program leaves the list once uninstalled.
programs.launched: uninstaller launched. Follow its steps: the list updates by itself.
report.title: Report for an AI
report.intro: Paste this report into the AI of your choice (ChatGPT, Claude…). It will ask you questions ("Do you still use…?") and then tell you what to delete to save the most space. Kleaner sends nothing.
report.privacy: It contains file, folder and program names (your user name is hidden). Read it before sharing.
report.copied: Copied: paste it into your AI.
analyse.fullAccess: Full scan: protected system folders included
analyse.topDirsChart: Where the space goes: 10 largest folders
cleanup.chartAdminHint: System and heavy cleanups are only counted in admin mode.
media.intro: All your videos (1 MB and up) and photos (50 KB and up) found by the last scan, excluding Windows and software folders. Sort, tick, send to the Recycle Bin.
media.needScan: Run a scan in the Scan tab first: the photo and video list comes from there.
sort.name: Name
viewer.unsupported: This format cannot be shown in Kleaner (MKV, AVI, HEIC, RAW…).
cleanup.showEmpty: Also show empty or not installed items
cleanup.nothing: Nothing to clean here right now.
verdict.open: What is it? Can I delete it?
verdict.title: What is it?
verdict.source.rule: Source: Kleaner knowledge base (knowledge.json on GitHub).
verdict.source.program: Source: the Programs list (this folder belongs to an installed program).
verdict.source.unknown: Kleaner never guesses: without a matching rule, the answer is « unknown ».
trash.criticalTitle: Careful: some of these files should not be deleted by hand.
trash.criticalAck: I understand the risk and still want to send them to the Recycle Bin
programs.lastUsedAdmin: Last launch comes from Windows Prefetch: run the full scan (admin) to see it.
drives.title: Drives to scan
drives.change: Choose drives for the next scan
about.tagline: Free, open-source and transparent Windows cleaner.
about.does.scan: Scans the drives you choose, hidden files included, and shows what takes up space.
about.does.clean: Removes caches and temporary files from its public catalog, after your confirmation.
about.does.explain: Explains what a file is and whether deleting it breaks something.
about.does.trash: Sends the personal files you pick to the Recycle Bin (recoverable).
about.does.log: Writes every action to a readable log.
about.never.sessions: Touch your passwords, cookies, sessions or history.
about.never.network: Connect to the Internet: no telemetry, no automatic updates.
about.never.admin: Ask for admin rights unless you click « Full scan (admin) ».
about.verdictsWarning: Verdicts (« safe », « breaks something »…) come from hand-written rules. They can be incomplete: when in doubt, keep the file.
about.linksNote: The buttons above open your web browser; Kleaner itself sends nothing.
dups.intro: Finds identical personal files (photos, videos, music, documents, archives, installers of 1 MB or more) among the last scan. Files are compared byte by byte; program files are never included.
dups.keepOldest: Tick all but the oldest copy
dups.lastCopy: Last copy: one copy always stays.
projects.intro: Dependency and build folders of your projects (node_modules, .venv, target, build…). Your tools recreate them, so old projects are an easy win. Deletion is permanent; your code is not touched.
projects.none: Nothing here: no project folder matches.
projects.permanent: Permanent deletion (not the Recycle Bin). Each project needs the command below before it runs again.
map.title: Disk map
map.hint: Each rectangle is a folder, sized by the space it takes. Click to go inside; folders under 64 MB are grouped.
preview.title: What would be deleted
preview.intro: Simulation: nothing has been deleted. Here is every file the selected cleanups would remove.
leftovers.title: Leftovers of uninstalled programs
leftovers.intro: Uninstallers usually keep their data in AppData. Kleaner lists folders that no installed program owns and that haven’t changed for 30 days.
leftovers.warning: Probable leftovers, not certain: a folder can belong to a tool that isn’t listed in Programs (command-line tools, portable apps). They go to the Recycle Bin, so you can restore them.
leftovers.adminOnly: In Program Files or ProgramData: Kleaner only reports it. Delete it from Explorer with admin rights if you are sure.
